Subject: Post-call recap & immediate ask — latency guardrails / token envelope

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side plus the concrete asks so we can size the SLO work and draft a Mutual Action Plan (attached):

- Goal: Integrate Redwood to power Strata's clinical-note summarization and triage assistant behind your VPC. Your key acceptance criteria are 95th pctile latency <= 450ms for 512-token outputs at 8 concurrent users and predictable degradation with streaming.
- Workloads discussed: bursty throughput during morning shift (est. 120 requests/min peak), mixed short (<=128 input tokens) and long (up to 6k input tokens) contexts, and multi-turn conversational state where KV cache reuse matters.
- Constraints: data residency in us-east-1, strict audit logs for PII, and on-prem connector for batch export.

Immediate asks from us to you:
1) Please confirm the target latency SLO (you mentioned 95p ~ 400–500ms). We need the final number to set routing policies and canary thresholds.
2) Share a representative sample prompt set (anonymized) and 3–5 long examples that hit the 4k–6k input window so we can run perf sims.
3) Confirm whether streaming output is required for incremental UI rendering (you indicated yes for triage UX).

Attachments: perf-matrix.xlsx (we sketched perf buckets / model variants), mutual-action-plan.pdf (high-level milestones).

Next steps from Redwood: we’ll run simulated load with your anonymized prompts and return a short matrix mapping model variant -> token envelope (input/output) -> expected 95p latency and recommended fallback routing.

Can you confirm the above and share the prompt samples by Tuesday 08/25?

Thanks —
Rishi
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate ask — latency guardrails / token envelope

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Confirming items below:

- Final SLO target: our product leadership wants 95p <= 450ms for the typical triage flow (input ~ 512 tokens, output capped at 512 tokens). We understand longer-context requests can have higher latencies but need a documented degradation curve.
- We will provide anonymized prompt samples (including 4 very long notes ~5k tokens) by EOD Tuesday.
- Streaming: yes — we need incremental output for the clinician UI so perceived latency is small even if full completion takes longer.

A few clarifying questions for your perf sims:
1) When you map model variants to token envelopes, can you include quantized variants (e.g., 4-bit) and expected accuracy delta?
2) For concurrency, our early rollout will have 8 concurrent interactive sessions per region, but planning for burst to ~40 concurrent in peak. Can your canary plan include a phasing of concurrency thresholds?

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min call if helpful.

—Elena
CTO, Strata Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & immediate ask — latency guardrails / token envelope

Marissa / Connor — forwarding Elena's confirmation and questions. Key asks to address in our perf sims and canary plan:

- Produce a matrix that includes: model variant (open-v1 / redwood-medium / quantized-4bit), typical token envelopes (input/output pairs), expected 95p latency at baseline concurrency (8) and at burst (40), and a short note on expected quality delta for quantized runs.
- Streaming behavior: simulate chunked delivery (every ~80 tokens) and measure first-byte latency and incremental completion times. Elena wants the UI to render partial results within ~120ms if possible.
- Circuit-breaker / fallback plan: recommend routing to a smaller variant or enabling partial streaming + cached prefix for very long contexts.

I've attached the perf-matrix.xlsx that has a starter template. Connor — can you own the perf sims (load generator + model variants) and populate the sheet? Marissa — can you draft the canary thresholds and a short blurb for the MAP on rollout phases and rollback triggers (e.g., 95p > 750ms -> immediate throttle / rollback)?

I'll coordinate with Elena on timing for the canary run next week once we have their sample prompts.

Rishi

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap & immediate ask — latency guardrails / token envelope

Thanks — I’ll take the perf sims. Quick notes on approach and assumptions so we can align before I run workloads:

- Test harness: will run a synthetic load driver that replays their anonymized prompts at controlled inter-arrival times and supports streaming traces. I’ll instrument for first-byte, median, 95p, and 99p latencies, as well as token throughput (tokens/sec) per GPU.
- Model/quantization candidates: open-v1 (FP16), redwood-medium (FP16), redwood-medium-4bit (quantized). I’ll include a small eval run to measure ROUGE/embedding-sim drop vs FP16 for the long-note set.
- Context handling: for long-context (~5k tokens) runs we’ll test two strategies: 1) full-context encode -> generate; 2) prefix-summarize (client-side) + incremental KV warm-starts to see latency savings and quality delta.
- Streaming: I’ll simulate chunk-size of 80 tokens and measure time-to-first-chunk and end-to-end completion. For the UI perceived-latency target (first chunk < 120ms), I’ll note which variant meets that under 8 concurrent and at burst 40.

I expect to have a populated perf-matrix.xlsx and a short memo for Marissa’s canary thresholds by EOD Wednesday 08/26. If their samples arrive late it’ll slide by 24–48 hours.

Connor
Senior Platform Engineer
Redwood Inference
